title: Levin's flatworm experiments read as morphic resonance

tellings.quote: conventional explanation of Levin's experiments my explanation would be that it was morphic resonance with the previous form of the intact form of the flat worm they resonating with themselves in the past

related.note: This is the same flatworm memory experiment as #9, but it puts forward morphic resonance in place of the conventional explanation.

plain: The biologist Rupert Sheldrake says the scientist Michael Levin's flatworm experiments at Tufts University, which look at how the worms recover their body form, are best explained by 'morphic resonance'. That is Sheldrake's idea that living things draw their forms from a kind of memory of earlier forms. On the show he says the worms are 'resonating with themselves in the past', with their earlier intact form, instead of following the conventional explanation, and if he is right, memory and form in living things would not be stored only in the body.
